article_title: GitHub Copilot Adds Dynamic Workflows, Code-Defined Multi-Agent Orchestration, to Its CLI, App and SDK

content_preview.title: GitHub Copilot Adds Dynamic Workflows, Code-Defined Multi-Agent Orchestration, to Its CLI, App and SDK
content_preview.summary: GitHub put dynamic workflows in public preview across Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and the Copilot SDK, letting developers define in code when agents run and how results are used.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub has made dynamic workflows available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app and the GitHub Copilot SDK, according to a [GitHub changelog entry dated October 1, 2026](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-dynamic-workflows-in-copilot-cli-and-the-copilot-app). The feature lets developers "define an orchestration in code to get the reliability and observability that complex, multi-agent work demands," in the changelog's words. It is in public preview.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of about 510 words (range 300-800). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure, neutral tone, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk (gunzip, text-extracted): source-0.html.gz (github.blog changelog, Oct 1, 2026, HTTP 200) and source-1.html.gz (docs.github.com concepts page, HTTP 200, full text on disk, not just a summarizer view). Both domains are allowlisted (github.blog; docs.github.com, first-party). suspicious_patterns null for both. source-0 confirms: date 'October 1, 2026'; 'Dynamic workflows are now available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot SDK'; 'define an orchestration in code to get the reliability and observability that complex, multi-agent work demands' (verbatim); 'A dynamic workflow is a program that defines how a task is carried out' (verbatim); steps sequential/parallel/both; 'The program itself lives inside a GitHub Copilot extension'; incident example and 'The same steps run every time'; 'agents handle the parts that need analysis or judgment'; 'Dynamic workflows are available on all Copilot plans.' (verbatim); app 'always available with no setup required'; CLI --experimental / '/experimental on' / '/update' / '/feedback'; 'Dynamic workflows are in public preview and subject to change.' (verbatim). source-1 confirms: public preview banner; same definition; 'Everything is defined in code'; autopilot 'keep working through a task without pausing to get your input'; /fleet 'Copilot decides how to break down the task each time'; dynamic workflow 'The workflow's author defines the steps, conditions, and handoffs'; four limits (concurrent agents, total agents, active running time, approximate AI credits) set in prompt, workflow code or personal settings with prompt taking priority; /workflows slash command and Workflows button in the app show runs, AI credit usage, and allow cancel/pause; 'a normal prompt in the standard chat mode is usually sufficient'; availability: 'available to users on all Copilot plans except Copilot Pro and Copilot Pro+ subscribers on existing annual plans who remain on legacy premium request-based billing.'
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every claim traces to the two cited sources. The plan-availability discrepancy is real and verbatim in both snapshots (changelog: all plans; docs: legacy annual Pro/Pro+ excluded); the article presents both statements under 'What We Don't Know' without choosing a side. The surfaces (CLI, app, SDK), public-preview status, and Oct 1, 2026 date are as stated. Absence of a GA date and of typical per-run cost on both pages is accurately reported. Vendor claims are attributed to GitHub / the changelog / the docs. The two internal /article/ links resolve to existing articles.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; the Analysis section is restrained and tied to cited wording.
editor_notes.originality: No prior article on dynamic workflows. Related recent Copilot coverage (computer use in CLI/app, Rust runtime rewrite) is different topics and is cross-linked by the article.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced briefing that handles the changelog/docs plan-availability disagreement transparently. Approved.
